description: Adds a perturbation step that jitters the SLSQP centres (Gaussian, sd 0.01) and re-optimises twice per restart, keeping the best result, to escape stalled local optima.
Adds a perturbation step that jitters the SLSQP centres (Gaussian, sd 0.01) and re-optimises twice per restart, keeping the best result, to escape stalled local optima.
Replaces the greedy repair with gradient descent on the radii to minimise the overlap penalty (centres fixed), followed by coordinate-ascent passes that keep the packing valid.
Gives SLSQP an analytic Jacobian for the objective and all constraints, with pair rows using the unit vector between centres, so each step is cheaper and more accurate than finite differences.

Adds two soft-penalty L-BFGS-B stages (overlap and wall violations penalised with increasing weight, radii free to overlap) before the existing SLSQP polish in _solve_once, so the search can pass through illegal states before the hard-constraint solve.

Splits the time budget into a 40% exploration phase of random-restart SLSQP runs and a 60% exploitation phase that repeatedly re-optimises the best packing found so far from a slightly jittered start.

After the first half of the random-restart budget, repeatedly move one random circle of the best packing to a random spot, re-optimise with SLSQP warm-started from that layout, and keep the result only if it beats the incumbent (basin-hopping jumps).

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The lambda inside the loop captures `pairs` late, but minimize runs inside the same iteration, so each solve gets the right value. The existing repair step still makes the packing valid.

This is a design flaw, not a bug that voids the result. With only the boundary constraints, maximising the sum of radii sends every circle towards radius 0.5 at centre (0.5, 0.5). This throws away the random start, so the second solve begins from a collapsed, degenerate point. That likely explains the drop to 2.9056.

Recomputed z from the rounded numbers: the loss difference is 0.0279. Taking sd = 0.0034 per run and 1 run on each side, the sd of the difference is 0.0034 x sqrt(2) = 0.00481, so z ≈ -5.80. The harness reports -5.739. The gap is small and could come from unrounded inputs or a slightly different sd. Either way the reject decision stands.
Evidence is weak: only 1 candidate run and 1 incumbent run. The effect is large, so rejecting is still justified.

description: Successive Constraint Addition: each SLSQP solve first optimises with only the wall/boundary constraints, then re-optimises from that result with the non-overlap constraints added.

Keeps a population of 3 packings, filled by random restarts, and every third iteration mutates the best one with the existing jump move; the mutant replaces the worst member only if its sum of radii is higher.

Before each random-restart SLSQP solve, run a short simulated annealing pass that moves single circle centres to maximise the minimum pairwise centre distance, so SLSQP starts from a less congested layout.

Before each random-restart SLSQP solve, run a short simulated annealing pass that moves single circle centres to maximise the minimum pairwise centre distance, so SLSQP starts from a less congested layout.

After each repaired SLSQP result, run 100 random local-search steps that jiggle all centres by Gaussian noise (sd 0.01), re-legalise the radii with the existing repair, and keep a move only if the sum of radii increases.

Elastic Band Repair: in _repair, each overlapping pair is pushed apart by half its overlap (centres clipped to the square, wall-limited radii recomputed) before the pair's radii are shrunk to the new distance.
Multi-stage cooling: each SLSQP solve runs three stages that allow overlap margins of 0.02, 0.01, then 0, warm-starting each stage from the previous one before the final exact-constraint solve.
Add Gaussian noise to the centres of the best-known packing at every random-restart iteration, then re-optimise.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. Randomness comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The change only affects the starting radii: they are now drawn from N(INIT_RADIUS, 0.02) and clipped to [0.005, 0.1]. SLSQP and the existing repair step still decide the final packing, so the validity checks are unchanged.
z recomputed as (2.9348 - 2.9335) / (0.0034 * sqrt(2)) = 0.0013 / 0.00481 ≈ 0.27. The harness reports 0.263, which matches within the rounding of the 4-decimal values.

The gain of 0.0013 is about 0.4 of one job's noise sd, and there is only one run per side, so the evidence is weak. Rejecting is consistent with the numbers. The cost of the change is small (a one-line change), so a replicate run could be worth one slot if improvements to the starting point are a priority.

description: Initialise each SLSQP start with normally distributed radii (mean 0.05, sd 0.02, clipped to [0.005, 0.1]) instead of a constant 0.05, to add variety in circle sizes at the start of each restart.

Scales the SLSQP maxiter with elapsed time so that random restarts later in the run get deeper optimisation (MAX_ITER times 1 plus the elapsed fraction of the budget), while the early restarts keep the original setting.
Runs SLSQP twice per solve, re-seeding the second run from the first result with Gaussian (sd 0.01) jitter on the centres, so each start is refined from a perturbed version of its own optimum.

Before each random-restart SLSQP solve, run L-BFGS-B on a soft-penalty objective (sum of radii minus lambda times squared overlap and wall violations) with lambda increasing over three stages, then hand the result to SLSQP.

After the time-budgeted restart/jump loop, polish the best packing with one extra SLSQP run using a larger iteration cap (500 instead of 200), then repair it and keep it only if its radius sum improves.

Replaces the uniform random initial centres of each SLSQP restart with a random subset of a hexagonal lattice over the unit square, jittered by Gaussian noise (sd 0.01), so the optimizer starts from a dense layout.
Starts each random-restart SLSQP from centres whose radii are all set to the largest uniform radius that keeps those centres non-overlapping and inside the square, with small random variation added.
Initialise each random-restart SLSQP start from centres relaxed by Lloyd iterations on a grid (a Voronoi centroidal tessellation of the unit square) instead of uniform random centres.
Initialise SLSQP starts from Voronoi-cell centroids with radii set to the distance to the nearest Voronoi edge.
Abort the population-based refinement idea: it repeats slot 8's population approach (rejected at +0.0019), and its circle-swap crossover between unrelated packings is unlikely to give valid gains.

Radius Diversity Constraints: random-restart SLSQP starts draw each circle's initial radius from a mix of large anchors (0.08, about 30%) and small fillers (0.03), replacing the uniform 0.05 start, so the optimiser begins with a spread of sizes that can fill gaps.
Scales SLSQP MAX_ITER with elapsed budget fraction (50 in the first 20%, 400 in the last 20%, 200 otherwise), threading a maxiter argument through _solve_once and _jump.
Replaces the uniform random initial centres of each random-restart SLSQP with a random subset of a staggered hexagonal grid, scaled into the square, with small Gaussian jitter on centres and radii.
Abort: the Overlap Penalty Gradient idea (soft overlap penalty with L-BFGS-B before SLSQP) repeats slots 4 and 17, which were already rejected.

After each SLSQP solve and repair, run 200 greedy local-search steps that pick a random circle, jitter its centre with a step size decaying from 0.05 to near 0, and keep the move only if the circle's feasible radius (limited by walls and neighbours) grows.
Optimise log-radii (r = exp(s)) inside SLSQP for both random restarts and the basin-hopping jump, so radii stay positive and scale-symmetric.

issues: No measurement gaming found. The diff only changes how the radii are parameterised: SLSQP now optimises log(r) instead of r. There is no file access, no pasted coordinates, and all randomness still comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that invalidates the result. The returned radii are exp(...), so they are always positive and the r >= 0 constraint is now redundant but harmless. The perturbation path guards log(0) with np.maximum(r, 1e-12). The exact validity check still applies to the final packing, and the repair step still receives radii on the normal scale.

Recomputed z from the given numbers: candidate mean -2.9388 (n=2), incumbent -2.9335 (n=1), difference 0.0053. Standard error = 0.0034*sqrt(1/2+1/1) ≈ 0.00416, so z ≈ 1.27. The harness reports 1.262. The small gap is probably rounding in the displayed values and does not change the decision.

Plausibility note: the candidate mean of 2.9388 is above the 2.9370 'best published' value on the program card. Newer results for n=32 of about 2.9395 have been reported, so this may be real. But a gain over a strong reference is worth checking: confirm that the harness's exact validity check ran on these packings. This is not grounds for a veto, because the harness reports no integrity flags.

The incumbent has only one run, so the comparison is weak. A replicate of the incumbent, or more candidate seeds, would settle whether this is a real improvement of about 0.005 in mean sum of radii. A provisional reject at z ≈ 1.27 matches the numbers.

issues: Measurement (1): nothing found. The diff only adds a greedy construction that places one circle at a time. Its randomness comes from the seed-based rng, it reads no files and contains no pasted coordinates, and the existing _repair step still runs on every restart.

Recomputed z: the candidate is 0.0021 better (-2.9356 vs -2.9335). The standard error is 0.0034 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/1) = 0.00481, so z = 0.0021 / 0.00481 = 0.44, matching the reported 0.435 up to rounding. This is far below a significance threshold, so the provisional reject is justified. Both arms have only one run each, so a replicate of each would be needed before claiming a gain.

Possible bug (2), not confirmed: the new code calls _solve_once(k, rng, x0) with a third argument. The diff does not show that _solve_once accepts a starting point. Since the job ran and returned a result, it apparently does.

Timing risk, not a veto: one sequential restart runs 32 SLSQP solves of growing size, and the time limit is only checked between restarts. One restart that starts late could push a call past the 45 s void limit. The job completed this time, but the margin is not guaranteed. Checking the time inside _sequential would make this safe.
Minor: building the arrays with np.vstack/np.append in a loop is fine at n=32.

description: Replaces the random-restart SLSQP start with a sequential greedy build that adds one circle at a time, re-optimising the packing after each addition from the previous solution.

Makes the slot-6 basin-hopping jump adaptive: the number of iterations between jumps halves after a jump that improves the best sum by more than 1e-3, doubles (capped at 8) after a marginal or negative one, and the iterations in between are random restarts.

Replaces the greedy best-only basin-hopping jumps with a Metropolis-accepted walk whose temperature cools linearly to zero over the jump phase, so worse packings can be kept early and only improvements late.
Aborted: combine the analytic SLSQP Jacobian with elastic-band repair, gated on SLSQP failure. Not tested.

Maintains a population of the top 5 packings, and after half the budget each iteration basin-hops from a randomly chosen member, with a fresh random-restart SLSQP every fourth iteration that competes for a slot in the population.

Abort: Parallel Restart Batching would shorten each random-restart SLSQP run to about 5 s so that more restarts fit in the budget, but this repeats the per-restart iteration-cap schedules already rejected in slots 15 and 23, and the "parallel" part cannot work on one CPU thread.
Combine the log-radii SLSQP formulation (s = ln r, with analytic objective and constraint Jacobians) with the slot-6 basin-hopping jump that moves one random circle after half the time budget.
Combine the log-radii SLSQP formulation (s = ln r, with analytic objective and constraint Jacobians) with the slot-6 basin-hopping jump that moves one random circle after half the time budget.

Abort Dynamic Radius Scaling: a global radius scale-up gains essentially nothing because repair already leaves almost no slack.

Initialises each random-restart SLSQP start from 32 uniform centres with radii set to half the nearest-neighbour distance (the distance to the nearest Voronoi edge), capped by the walls, instead of the constant INIT_RADIUS.

Before each random-restart SLSQP solve, run a 150-step Metropolis annealing pass that jitters one centre at a time, scored by the largest valid radii, and keep the slot-6 basin-hopping jumps after half the budget.
